contexts.text: A ruby, a topaz, and a carbuncle () = the celestial love of good... on account of their red and flaming colour... here, celestial love, because they are in the first row... Hence these three stones represent the Inmost Heaven, and consequently the love there...
The ruby, which is in the first place, in the Original Language, is derived from a word which means redness.
Hence, the Word, in its ultimate bosom, from its natural sense in which are the two interior ones, is like a ruby and a diamond: from celestial flame, like a ruby...
The Divine sphere which encompasses the Lord... appears, in the Celestial Kingdom, glowing red like a ruby...
The bride (wore) on her head a crown of gold studded with rubies.
(She wore) a stomacher fastened in front with rubies.
The furniture of their houses... flashed with gold as if flaming from the interstudded rubies.
These three degrees are distinct from each other as... are a ruby, a sapphire, and an agate. Moreover... a ruby, in the Word, = celestial good, which is the good of the highest Heaven.
That a ruby is so called from redness. Illustrated. Hence it is that by a ruby is signified the truth of celestial good.
